purpose: Insulin detemir is used to help control blood sugar levels in people with type 1 or type 2 diabetes. It is a background insulin that works slowly throughout the day or night to keep your blood sugar steady between meals and while you sleep. It is not meant to cover blood sugar spikes from meals.
how_it_works: Your body normally makes insulin to help sugar from your blood get into your cells for energy. Insulin detemir works just like your body's own insulin but is designed to be absorbed slowly and steadily after injection. This gives you a long, even level of insulin activity for up to 24 hours, helping keep your blood sugar from going too high between meals.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is low blood sugar (hypoglycemia), which can cause shakiness, sweating, dizziness, confusion, or hunger — so always have a fast-acting sugar source nearby. You may also notice redness, swelling, or itching at the injection site. Some people gain a little weight while using insulin.
warnings: Never share your insulin pen or needles with anyone else, even if the needle is changed, as this can spread serious infections. Do not use insulin detemir during episodes of low blood sugar. Avoid injecting into the same spot every time to prevent skin thickening. Tell your doctor right away if you have kidney or liver problems, are pregnant, or are planning to become pregnant, as your insulin dose may need to change. Always check the label — do not mix this insulin with other insulins in the same syringe.
typical_dosing: Insulin detemir is injected under the skin (usually in the stomach, thigh, or upper arm) once or twice a day. Your doctor will tell you exactly how many units to take and when to take it based on your blood sugar levels and needs. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as dosing is very individual.
